text: . Global crude oil prices reversed earlier gains today. Brent crude was trading 0.8 per cent down at 90 US dollars per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.7 per cent down at 83 US dollars and 83 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. India’s total exports reached a record 863.1 billion US dollars in the financial year 2025-26. The government informed Parliament yesterday that the surge was driven by strong growth in both merchandise and services exports and supported by expanding market access under the country’s free trade agreements (FTAs).According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, merchandise exports stood at 441.8 billion dollars, while services exports reached 421.3 billion dollars, reflecting the combined strength of both sectors in driving the country’s export growth. The Ministry said India’s recent trade agreements have significantly expanded export opportunities, particularly with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the United Kingdom, Australia, Oman and EFTA countries, while also helping diversify export markets and strengthen labour-intensive sectors.Among FTA partners, merchandise exports in the financial year 2025-26 were highest to ASEAN countries at 38.42 billion dollars, followed by the UAE at 37.36 billion dollars, SAFTA countries, the UK and Singapore. The Ministry highlighted the growing utilisation of India’s recently operationalised trade agreements through the increasing use of Certificates of Origin and wider product coverage.

. The Nation pays homage to revolutionary freedom fighter Shaheed Udham Singh on his 87th martyrdom day today.Belonging to Ghadar Party and Hindustan Socialist Republic Association, Udham Singh assassinated Michael O’Dwyer, former Lieutenant Governor of British Punjab on 13th March 1940 to take revenge of 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre of Amritsar.The disturbing memory of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre kept haunting him till the time he shot Michael O’Dwyer dead in London’s Caxton Hall.While in custody, he used the name ‘Ram Mohammad Singh Azad’, representing the three major religions in India and his anti-colonial sentiment. He was convicted of murder and hanged on this day in 1940.To commemorate the martyrdom of the legendary revolutionary, a state-level programme will be organised at his birth place Sunam in Punjab. Haryana government is also paying tributes to him at a programme in Sanaur, today.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended with modest gains today. The Sensex rose 274 points or 0.35 percent  to close at 77,928, while Nifty added 67 points or 0.3 percent to settle at 24,317.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index dropped over 0.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index fell nearly 0.6 percent.Earlier, the markets opened on a subdued note as rising crude oil prices and escalating tensions in West Asia weighed on investor sentiment. After remaining range-bound for most of the session, both benchmark indices edged higher during the final hour of trading.In the Sensex pack, 15 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Maruti climbed nearly 1.8 per cent, Mahindra and Mahindra rose over 1.7 per cent and Reliance added over 1.4 per cent. In contrast, Adani Ports shed almost 3.3 per cent, Indigo dipped 0.9 per cent and Bajaj Finserv lost 0.8 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 16 out of 27 sectors ended in negative zone. Among the top laggards, Realty dipped 2.1 per cent, Housing Finance slipped 1.3 per cent, and MidSmall Private Banks Quality Tilt fell 0.8 per cent. In contrast, Auto rose 1.6 per cent, Energy advanced over 0.7 per cent, and Consumer Discretionary gained half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2 thousand 630 companies declined, 1 thousand 601 advanced, and 176 remained unchanged.

. In Commonwealth Games, Indian Weightlifter Lovepreet Singh won a silver medal in the men’s 110 kg category while Seema Kaliramna bagged a bronze medal in women’s discus throw at Glasgow last night. Australia continued to lead the standings with 110 medals while India were 10th with 17 medals on Day 8. India’s medal count includes three gold, 10 silver and four bronze.India’s Lovepreet set the Games record in snatch and narrowly missed out on the gold medal. Lovepreet lifted a Games record 176kg in the snatch before managing 212kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 388kg. New Zealand’s David Liti won gold with 389kg while England’s Andrew Griffiths took the bronze medal with a total of 356kg.In women’s discus throw, Seema Kaliramna clinched a bronze medal with 58.65 meter while compatriot Nidhi Rani finished fourth. Jamaica’s Samantha Hall won the gold with a Games-leading throw of 61.66 meter, while Canada’s Julia Tunks took silver with 60.67 meter.Earlier in the day, Neeraj Chopra qualified for men’s javelin throw finals. Javelin throwers Rohit Yadav and Yashvir Singh have also entered the finals. Neeraj finished fifth, Rohit Yadav 9th and Yashvir Singh 10th in the qualification round.Two Indian triple jumpers, Praveen Chithravel and Selva Prabhu Thirumaran advanced to the final. Tejaswin Shankar also remained in medal contention in the men’s decathlon, ending the opening day in second place with 4,339 points after five events.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by three paise to end at 95 rupees and 68 paise against the US dollar.

. India has strongly condemned recent attacks on several maritime vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, saying that targeting commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end.Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, said that after a brief pause in the ongoing conflict in the region, there has been a worrying resumption of attacks and escalation of hostilities. Mr Harish voiced India’s strong condemnation of attacks on several vessels, including GFS Galaxy, MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa, during their transit through the Strait of Hormuz this month. He said that free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored.

. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat Gold was trading 0.4 per cent up at 1,43,340 rupees per 10 grams, while Silver was trading over 0.6 per cent up at 2,19,580 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the August contract was trading over half a per cent up at 1,42,582 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the September contract was trading 0.4 per cent up at 2,18,303 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.

. The Supreme Court today directed the Delhi government to provide proper medical treatment to persons injured by the alleged use of pellet guns during recent students’ protest in the national capital. The three judge bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was hearing a plea alleging the use of metallic pellet guns on students protesting at Jantar Mantar and other parts of Delhi.During the hearing, the bench said that police rules permit the use of pellet guns in exceptional circumstances and said that unless the rules themselves are challenged, the use of such weapons cannot be considered illegal.The petitioners sought a direction to phase out or prohibit the use of metallic or partially metallic kinetic projectiles fired from pump-action rifles and projectile-action guns for dispersing civilian crowds during law enforcement operations. The petition also sought directions to ensure comprehensive medical treatment, long-term care, and rehabilitation for the victims.

. In squash, the Indian men’s team has stormed into the semi-finals of the Squash Junior Team Championships in Ontario, Canada. The fifth-seeded Indian men’s team defeated England 2-1 to reach the semi-finals. They will next face the United States, which advanced to the last four after defeating Japan.Meanwhile, the women’s team lost 1-2 to the United States in the quarter-finals. History was rewritten as France’s men’s team reached the semi-finals of the World Squash Junior Team Championships for the first time in 26 years.

. In Taipei Open Badminton, Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag, Tanvi Sharma and Kiran George have progressed to the Singles quarter-finals. However, Anmol Kharb and HS Prannoy crashed out in second round matches today.Unnati Hooda defeated Tanya Hemanth 21-19, 21-12 in an all-Indian tie. Tanvi Sharma defeated Indonesia’s Thalita Wiryawan 21-17, 22-20 to reach the last eight. Devika Sihag made it three Indians in the women’s singles quarters, beating Indonesia’s Ni Kadek Dhinda Pratiwi 21-16, 21-15. Devika and Unnati will face each other in the top eight. Kiran George kept the Indian challenge alive in men’s singles. He won the other all-Indian clash of the day against Tharun Mannepalli 21-15, 21-16.

. The government has said that the country became free from Left Wing Extremism after nearly six decades of violence, which was once considered one of the biggest threats to internal security.In reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha,  Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said that this has been achieved with resolute implementation of the National Policy and Action Plan to address Left-Wing Extremism 2015 and the coordinated efforts of Centre and State governments. He informed the House that at present, no district is categorized as LWE affected. Mr Rai added that the number of Naxal-affected districts reduced from 126 to 90 in April 2018, 70 in July 2021, 38 in April 2024, 8 in December 2025 and zero in March 2026.The Minister also informed that  at present, 37 districts are categorized as Legacy and Thrust districts, which are no more LWE affected, but continued support regarding security and development measures is required for some more time to consolidate the position. He informed that one district has been kept under the category of District of Concern where LWE violent activities have been totally contained and their organizational structure has been completely dismantled.The Minister said that in the post-LWE scenario, the focus is on saturation of government welfare programmes, strengthening local self-governance, facilitating the rehabilitation of surrendered cadres and expanding the reach of governance and public services in remote areas. Mr Rai said that overall, Centre is committed for ensuring security and accelerated development of erstwhile LWE affected districts of the country.

. The United States and Iran exchanged fresh waves of missile strikes today, raising fears of a wider regional conflict and dimming hopes for a quick resolution. After a brief lull in hostilities, the renewed attacks have heightened concerns that the fighting could draw in more countries.Jordan said it intercepted five Iranian missiles for the second consecutive day. Kuwait reported that an Iranian strike hit a building belonging to a Chinese company in the country’s north, killing one person and causing extensive damage. Earlier this week, drone attacks sparked fires on ships at an Egyptian port, while Saudi Arabia said it had come under attack from Iran-backed militias in Iraq.The latest escalation follows a major wave of US strikes on Iran, launched in response to an earlier Iranian missile attack on a US military base in Jordan. US Central Command said it targeted dozens of Revolutionary Guard sites, including military command centres, missile and drone facilities, and coastal surveillance and defence installations. Iranian state media said three people were killed and two others injured in a strike on Qeshm Island.The latest exchange comes a day after the United States, in coordination with Saudi Arabia, carried out strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq, reportedly killing at least 20 fighters and six Iranian military advisers.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah today paid tribute to revolutionary martyr Udham Singh on his martyrdom day.Sharing a Sanskrit quote in a social media post, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the life of martyr Udham Singh, marked by his extraordinary courage and sacrifice, will continue to inspire every generation of the nation to safeguard the country’s honour and sovereignty.In a social media post, the Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that martyr Udham Singh’s indomitable courage and the sacrifice he made in the efforts to free India are a glorious chapter in Indian history. Mr Singh remarked that the nation will not only remember his sacrifice but will also continue to draw inspiration from him forever.In a social media post, Amit Shah described Udham Singh as a symbol of unparalleled courage and valour. He said the revolutionary avenged the victims of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre by eliminating Michael O’Dwyer in London, sending a strong message to the British regime. Mr Shah also said that through the Ghadar Party, Udham Singh played a significant role in kindling the spirit of freedom among Indians living abroad.The Home Minister said the life of martyr Udham Singh, embracing the noose of the gallows with a smile for the sake of independence, stands as an unmatched example of patience, resolve, and patriotism.

. Rebel TMC MP Saayoni Ghosh attended the NDA Parliamentary Party’s ‘Mangal Milan’ meeting for the first time. Speaking to Reporters at Parliament premises, she described the experience as enriching and said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address focused on the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), the Blue Economy and the government’s vision for country’s future.

. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) today claimed that its Aerospace Force targeted a US air base and the US Central Command (CENTCOM) headquarters in Jordan with ballistic missiles.The IRGC said the strikes were carried out in response to US military attacks on Iran and vowed to continue operations until US threats, illegal and hostile moves end, the official Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported. The claim comes amid renewed tensions in West Asia following military exchanges between Iran and the US.Meanwhile, the US military said it intercepted multiple ballistic missiles launched from Iran in what it described as an attempted “surprise attack” on American forces in the region.US Central Command said on X that , Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East in an attempted surprise attack. It added that all missiles were intercepted and US forces remained on high alert.

. India Meteorological Department has issued a severe weather warning, forecasting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across widespread parts of Gujarat over the next forty-eight hours. Fishermen have been strictly advised not to venture into the sea till August 1. Our correspondent reports that the state administration remains on alert and all the precautionary measures are being taken.The monsoon situation in Gujarat remains critical, as the IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy rainfall for 13 districts today, covering Central and South Gujarat, including Ahmedabad, Anand, Surat, Navsari, and Valsad. Authorities and disaster management teams remain on high readiness across all high-risk areas.Schools and colleges in several affected districts, including Ahmedabad and Navsari, will remain closed today as a precautionary measure. Meanwhile, the state government has issued strict instructions to district administrations to ensure the speedy evacuation of residents living in low-lying and flood-prone areas to shelter homes.

. Saudi Arabia and 13 other countries have established a maritime defence coalition aimed at protecting shipping in key waterways of West Asia. The announcement came after military figures from dozens of countries met in Riyadh to discuss the alliance. A joint statement issued by the alliance said that the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition aims to tackle the growing challenges facing global maritime security.It said the alliance will serve as a framework for maritime defence cooperation, aimed at enhancing maritime security, protecting freedom of navigation, securing international trade routes and energy supply lines. The alliance is part of efforts to safeguard shared maritime interests in Bab El-Mandeb Strait, Red Sea, and Gulf of Aden, in accordance with the provisions of international law.The founding members of the coalition include Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Yemen, Nigeria, Sudan, Djibouti, and Somalia. Member states said the coalition is purely defensive in nature, does not target any state, alliance, or international organisation, and conducts all its activities in full compliance with international law, respect for state sovereignty, and the protection of freedom of navigation. They agreed that Saudi Arabia is the founding and leading state of the coalition and serves as its permanent headquarters.

. Most Asian stock markets declined today. South Korea’s Kospi index fell over 1.2 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index dropped 0.7 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 0.6 per cent, and Taiwan’s Taiex slipped over 0.2 per cent. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.7 per cent and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index added 0.2 per cent. Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan’s two-day policy meeting commenced today.On economic front, the euro area economy grew 0.4 per cent and by 0.5 per cent in the EU during the second quarter on a sequential basis, according to preliminary flash estimate published by Eurostat.Major European indices were trading with gains today. France’s CAC 40 gained one per cent, London’s FTSE 100 increased by 0.4 per cent, and Germany’s DAX added 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in.Meanwhile, the Bank of England voted to hold interest rates steady at 3.75 per cent. However, three members of the Monetary Policy committee voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4 per cent.

. The Union Health Ministry today observed World Hepatitis Day 2026, marking 8 years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). The programme, launched in 2018 under the National Health Mission, aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals.Addressing the event in New Delhi, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to achieving a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat. She said India is among the few countries providing free treatment for Hepatitis C and free management of Hepatitis B. She added that hepatitis screening and treatment services have now been expanded to more than one lakh 85 thousand Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, improving access to care across the country.The Minister said Hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination coverage has crossed 92 per cent. She urged States and Union Territories to ensure 100 per cent screening of pregnant women for Hepatitis B and to step up awareness on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C for early detection and timely treatment. On the occasion, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said that under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme, over 21 crore people have been screened, more than six lakh patients treated and one thousand 153 treatment centres established across the country. She added that over seven crore 64 lakh pregnant women have also been screened under the programme.During the event, the Ministry also released Information, Education and Communication materials on viral hepatitis, highlighting its modes of transmission and the services available under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme for wider dissemination across States and Union Territories.

. In squash, India’s men and women teams advanced to the quarterfinals of the World Junior Squash Team Championships in Ontario, Canada. The fifth-seeded Indian men defeated 11th-seeded Kuwait 2-1 in the pre-quarterfinals .Yusha Nafees lost the opening match in straight games to Abdullah Ali, but Aryaveer Dewan leveled the tie with an 11-5, 11-6, 11-5 victory over Khaled Walead Al Fouzain. Gurveer Singh then sealed the win with an 11-3, 11-3, 11-4 triumph against Abdul Rahman Al Sanea. India will face England in the quarterfinals.The Indian women completed the group stage with a dominant 3-nil win over South Africa. Rudra Singh defeated Makayla Naidoo 11-4, 11-5, 11-3 before Anahat Singh cruised past Brianna Robinson 11-1, 11-1, 11-3. Saanvi Kalanki completed the sweep with an 11-4, 11-3, 11-3 victory over Vivienne Van Der Schyff. India’s women will take on the United States in the quarterfinals.

. Protests continued in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) today following a brutal crackdown by Pakistani security forces on civilians earlier this week, which left more than 40 people dead. Local authorities in the occupied region have now allegedly begun targeting women protesters demanding basic rights. Pakistani security forces opened fire on women demonstrators gathered in large numbers in Rawalakot and Mirpur, where they were raising slogans against the crackdown. Several videos circulating on social media purportedly show women fleeing as police opened fire during a peaceful protest rally in Kotli. Analysts claim that the total number of people killed since the protests began may have crossed 125.In a statement issued, Spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Jeremy Laurence, said that the criminalisation of a civil society organisation and imposition of strict limitations on gatherings in POJK raise serious concerns about infringements on the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association.The tensions coincide with so called ongoing regional elections in the occupied territory, with demonstrators determined to march towards Muzaffarabad to press Islamabad to accept their demands.India has described the elections as an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave human rights violations in the region.

. India scripted history in para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, securing a historic one-two finish in the men’s 100-metre T47 final, with Dilip Mahadu Gavit winning gold and Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath claiming silver.Gavit clocked a Games record and season-best time of 10.71 seconds to take the top spot, while Basil produced his season-best time of 10.83 seconds to finish second in a closely fought race. England’s Kevin Santos completed the podium with 10.85 seconds to win the bronze medal.These medals were India’s third and fourth medals of the day, after long jumper Murali Sreeshankar had earlier opened the day’s account with a silver in the men’s long jump. The silver medal also made Sreeshankar the first Indian men’s long jumper to win two Commonwealth Games medals.The gold was India’s third at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, following Mirabai Chanu’s victory in the women’s 48-kilogram weightlifting event and Sharmila Dhankar’s triumph in the women’s shot put F57 para athletics category. The medals lifted India to eighth spot in the standings, taking its overall tally to 15 medals — three gold, nine silver and three bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Dilip Mahadu Gavit on winning the Gold Medal and Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 100-metre T47 event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026.

. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) has charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activities and has started the process of placing him on the international wanted list, according to Russian state media.The FSB alleges that Telegram failed to remove channels, chats and bots that were allegedly used by Ukrainian intelligence to plan attacks inside Russia. Authorities also claim that Telegram’s dating service was used to recruit Russians for terrorist activities. It is also said that an international warrant for his arrest has been issued.According to Russian legal experts, Durov could face arrest in absentia as part of the legal process to seek his extradition through Interpol. Russian media also reported that the charges could carry a life sentence if he is convicted. Durov has not publicly responded to these latest charges.Durov has previously faced legal action in France over allegations related to illegal content on Telegram, including child sexual abuse material, fraud and drug trafficking.

. Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that safety is accorded the highest priority on Indian Railways and as a consequence of various safety measures taken over the years, there has been a steep decline in the number of accidents. In a written reply in the Lok Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said, after extensive and elaborate trials, Kavach Version 4.0 has been successfully commissioned on two thousand 569 Route Kilometres covering the high density Delhi- Mumbai and Delhi-Howrah routes as on 20th of this month. He informed that the funds utilized on Kavach works so far up to last month is three thousand 874 Crore rupees. Mr Vaishnaw said, the allocation of funds during the year 2026-27 is two thousand 66 crore rupees. He said, Kavach work is going at a good pace in the entire country. The Minister said, specialized training programmes on Kavach are being conducted at centralized training institutes of Indian Railways to impart training to all concerned officials. He said, by now more than 94 thousand technicians, operators and engineers have been trained on Kavach technology. He added that this includes about 57 thousand Loco Pilots and Assistant Loco Pilots.

. Parliament has passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 with the Rajya Sabha approving it yesterday. The Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on Wednesday. When the House reassembled post-lunch, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh moved the bill. Chairman C P Radhakrishnan said that seven hours have been allocated for the discussion on the bill.The legislation incorporates several significant provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment for up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees, and the seizure of the properties of convicted offenders. To ensure the expeditious disposal of cases, the legislation mandates that every State Government and Union Territory Administration establish Special Fast Track Courts for the day-to-day trial.It further provides that investigations into offences must be completed within two months from the date the information is recorded at the police station. The trials must be concluded within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.Replying to the discussion on the Bill, Minister of State for Personnel and PMO, Dr Jitendra Singh, said this issue touches every citizen of India and has stake with every citizen of this country. Mr. Singh also listed the government’s efforts to prevent paper leaks and to reform the education system in the country. He said youth are a huge investment for a Viksit Bharat. The Minister said the number of AIIMS hospitals has increased from 7 to 22, and medical seats have also increased.He said this is democratisation through accessibility and affordability of medical education. He said National Education Policy 2020 has been the biggest game changer over the last decade. He added that it has liberated adolescent children from the slavery of the subjects chosen by their parents or guardians in Class 12. The Opposition staged a walkout as the Minister was replying to the discussion.Earlier, moving the Bill in the House, Dr Jitendra Singh said that this Bill is a reaffirmation of the government’s highest commitment to safeguard the welfare of the students and youth of this country. He said, under the new legislation, the investigation must be completed within two months and the trial within three months after filing the charge sheet. Dr Singh said, the paper leaks are a serious issue and several incidents were reported from various parts of the country in different State governments and the previous governments at the centre.Dr Singh reiterated the Modi government’s resolve of zero tolerance towards malpractices and paper leaks of public examinations. Dr Singh said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi lost no time in bringing this bill, reflecting the government’s commitment that nobody will be allowed to jeopardise the future of the students.Initiating the discussion, Leader of the Opposition Malikarjun Kharge said the government has made only cosmetic changes in the new bill and the proposed amendments will not be effective to curb malpractices in the public examinations. He said, though the Congress supports the proposed bill but it lacks very stringent provisions to ensure transparent and paper-leak-free examinations. Mr Kharge said that the government took this step only after students raised concerns about the paper leak, irregularities in examinations, and institutional failures.Participating in the discussion, Brij Lal of BJP said that the government has proposed amendment to the 2024 Act to make very stringent provisions to curb unfair means and malpractices in public examinations. He said the intention of the Narendra Modi government is very clear that provisions have been incorporated in the bill to establish fast track courts for speedy trials. He added that for investigation of cases, there is a provision of constituting Special Task Force.Tiruchi Siva of DMK demanded abolition of NEET Exam. He claimed that the amended legislation will not change the education system in the country.Supporting the Bill, Sanjay Kumar Jha of JD(U) said the NDA government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has taken several landmark initiatives in terms of medical education.Ram Gopal Yadav of Samajawadi Party said only increasing punishment will not prevent the crime from happening. He demanded abolition of NEET exam saying that states should be given the power to conduct entrance exams for medical education.Supporting the legislation, Praful Patel of NCP said, everyone including the Government and opposition, is serious about the future of the students and the youth. He also called for the correct guidance for the youth. He supported the democratic right to protest but raised questions on the kind of language used during the protests.Sanjay Singh of AAP highlighted the backlog of cases in fast-track courts and the lack of facilities in education and schools.BJP’s Sudhanshu Trivedi said NEET exams have levelled the playing field for all students, and it is inspiring to see students from economically weaker sections do well in NEET exams. He alleged that the Opposition is trying to misguide the youth.Congress MP Mukul Wasnik said merely increasing punishment, amount of fine, and setting up fast-track courts will not bring transparency, fairness, and credibility to the exams.Sagarika Ghose of TMC, M Thambidurai of AIADMK, Y V Subba Reddy of YSRCP, Santrupt Misra of BJD, Manoj Jha of RJD, John Brittas of CPI(M), and Union Minister and RPI leader Ramdas Athawale also participated in the discussion among others.Later, the House was adjourned for the day to meet again at 11 am today.

. India’s boxing juggernaut rolled on at the Commonwealth Games as reigning world champion Jaismine Lamboria stormed into the women’s 57 kg semifinals with a hard-fought victory over England’s Elise Glynn today, assuring the country of yet another medal. Displaying tactical maturity, composure and sharp counter-punching, Lamboria edged the closely contested quarterfinal to become the 10th Indian boxer to secure at least a bronze medal in Glasgow with the semi finals scheduled for Friday.The victory extends India’s remarkable boxing campaign, with the contingent now guaranteed double-digit medals.Earlier, Preeti Pawar (54kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Sakshi Choudhary (51kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Lovlina Borgohain (75kg), Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (55kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg) and Narender Berwal (90 kg) had also booked semifinal berths.National record holder Animesh Kujur clocked his season’s best time to qualify for the 200 metre semifinals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow today.The 23-year-old Kujur clocked 20.46 seconds to win Heat 4 of the first round, finishing ahead of Cameroon’s Emmanuel Eseme, who had clinched the 100m gold yesterday with a time of 9.83 seconds.Kujur qualified seventh overall among the 16 semifinalists, while Eseme, who recorded 20.73 seconds in the heats, advanced in 14th place.The 16 fastest from across 10 heats advanced to the semi-finals to be held tomorrow.

. The Digital India BHASHINI Division under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology today conducted a Multilingual AI Workshop for officials of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Secretariat to promote language-first legislative governance. The workshop showcased AI-powered language technologies aimed at making legislative processes more inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric.The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology said, the workshop brought together Members of the Legislative Assembly, Assembly Secretariat officials and other stakeholders to explore how multilingual Artificial Intelligence can improve legislative workflows, enhance access to legislative information and enable seamless communication across languages.Speaking on the occasion, Chief Executive Officer of the Digital India BHASHINI Division, Amitabh Nag, said BHASHINI aims to build a language-first Digital Public Infrastructure where every citizen can access digital public services in the language they understand the best. He said multilingual AI can help legislative institutions improve efficiency through real-time transcription, translation, multilingual publication and better citizen engagement.The Ministry said the workshop marks another step towards expanding the adoption of AI-powered language technologies across public institutions and strengthening multilingual, transparent and citizen-centric governance.

. A delegation from Bastar Mandal of Chhattisgarh comprising winners of Bastar Pandum 2026, Pargana Manjhi and Chalaki of Bastar and Padma awardees, called on President Droupadi Murmu today at Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre. The President felicitated the members of the delegation and interacted with them. Union Minister for Home Affairs and Cooperation, Amit Shah, and Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Vishnu Deo Sai were present on the occasion.Speaking on the occasion, the President emphasized that events like Bastar Pandum have played an important role in reconnecting the youth with their traditions, customs, and cultural heritage. President Murmu highlighted that such events promote tourism and create employment opportunities. The President noted that the transformation in Bastar is a source of joy and pride for the entire nation. She expressed confidence that people of Chhattisgarh will scale new heights of development, peace and prosperity through their collective strength and determination. Further, President Murmu assured them that the government would stand by them in every situation.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today paid homage to Hindi litterateur Munshi Premchand on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Shah described Munshi Premchand as the “Emperor of Stories”.He said that Munshi Premchand portrayed events in his literary works with such vividness that they continue to feel alive even today. The Home Minister said that while Munshi Premchand gave voice to society’s pain, inequalities and exploitation through his writings, he also portrayed the sensitivities of children in a simple yet impactful manner through his children’s stories.Mr Shah added that even today, Munshi Premchand’s literary works remain the finest source of inspiration and guidance for understanding ideal writing.

. The 135th edition of the Durand Cup will begin in Shillong today. The city will host the Group E matches at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.Shillong is all set to host the Group E matches of the 135th edition of Durand Cup today. The Group features three football clubs from Meghalaya namely the Shillong Lajong, Nongkseh Sports, Social & Cultural Club and the Langsning Football Club, making the competition even more exciting for local football fans. The Mumbay Football Club is also part of the Group E matches.Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma will attend the opening ceremony which is slated for this afternoon. A series of performances including one by the military band has been lined up for the cultural programme. Additionally, the Indian Armed Forces have set up a display of weapons and equipment, which will remain open to the general public from 10 AM to 7 PM at the Polo Ground here today. The display will again be open to public on the 3rd of August.

. Parliament has passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 with the Rajya Sabha approving it today. The Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha yesterday. When the House reassembled post-lunch, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh moved the bill. Chairman C P Radhakrishnan said that seven hours have been allocated for the discussion on the bill.The legislation incorporates several significant provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment for up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees, and the seizure of the properties of convicted offenders. To ensure the expeditious disposal of cases, the legislation mandates that every State Government and Union Territory Administration establish Special Fast Track Courts for the day-to-day trial. It further provides that investigations into offences must be completed within two months from the date the information is recorded at the police station. The trials must be concluded within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.Replying to the discussion on the Bill, Minister of State for Personnel and PMO, Dr Jitendra Singh said this issue touches every citizen of India and has stake with every citizen of this country. Mr. Singh also listed the government’s efforts to prevent paper leaks and to reform the education system in the country. He said youth are a huge investment for a Viksit Bharat. The Minister said the number of AIIMS hospitals has increased from 7 to 22, and medical seats have also increased. He said this is democratisation through accessibility and affordability of medical education. He said National Education Policy 2020 has been the biggest game changer over the last decade. He added that it has liberated adolescent children from the slavery of the subjects chosen by their parents or guardians in Class 12.Meanwhile, the Opposition staged a walkout as the Minister was replying to the discussion.Earlier, moving the Bill in the House, Dr Jitendra Singh said that this Bill is a reaffirmation of the government’s highest commitment to safeguard the welfare of the students and youth of this country. He said, under the new legislation, the investigation must be completed within two months and trial within three months after filing the charge sheet. Dr Singh said, the paper leaks are a serious issue, and several incidents were reported from various parts of the country in different state governments and the previous governments at the centre. Dr Singh reiterated the Modi government’s resolve of zero tolerance towards  malpractices and paper leaks of public examinations. Dr Singh said, ‘Prime Minister Narendra Modi lost no time in bringing this bill reflecting the government’s commitment  that nobody will be allowed to jeopardise future of the students.Initiating the discussion, Leader of the Opposition Malikarjun Kharge said the government has made only cosmetic changes in the new bill and the proposed amendments will not be effective to curb malpractices in the public examinations. He said, though the Congress supports the proposed bill but it lacks very stringent provisions to ensure transparent and paper-leak-free examinations.’ Mr Kharge said that the government took this step only after students raised concerns about the paper leak, irregularities in examinations, and institutional failures.Participating in the discussion, Brij Lal of BJP said that the government has proposed an amendment to the 2024 Act to make very stringent provisions to curb unfair means and malpractices in public examinations. He said the intention of the Narendra Modi government is very clear that provisions have been incorporated in the bill to establish fast track courts for speedy trials. He added that for investigation of cases, there is a provision of constituting Special Task Force.Tiruchi Siva of DMK demanded abolition of NEET Exam. He claimed that the amended legislation will not change the education system in the country.Supporting the Bill, Sanjay Kumar Jha of JD(U) said the NDA government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has taken several landmark initiatives in terms of medical education.Ram Gopal Yadav of Samajawadi Party said only increasing punishment will not prevent the crime from happening. He demanded abolition of NEET exam saying that states should be given the power to conduct entrance exams for medical education.Supporting the legislation, Praful Patel of NCP said, everyone including the Government and opposition are serious about the future of the students and the youth. He also called for the correct guidance for the youth. He supported the democratic right to protest but raised questions on the kind of language used during the protests.Sanjay Singh of AAP highlighted the backlog of cases in fast-track courts and the lack of facilities in education and schools.BJP’s Sudhanshu Trivedi said NEET exams have levelled the playing field for all students and it is inspiring to see students from economically weaker sections do well in NEET exams. He alleged that Opposition is trying to misguide the youth.Congress MP Mukul Wasnik said merely increasing punishment, amount of fine, and setting up fast track courts will not bring transparency, fairness and credibility to the exams.Sagarika Ghose of TMC, M Thambidurai of AIADMK, Y V Subba Reddy of YSRCP, Santrupt Misra of BJD, Manoj Jha of RJD, John Brittas of CPI(M), and Union Minister and RPI leader Ramdas Athawale also participated in the discussion among others.Later, the House was adjourned for the day to meet again at 11 am tomorrow.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today chaired a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CSS) to review the situation in the context of on-going West Asia conflict and measures taken by various Ministries and Departments. Addressing the meeting, Mr Modi called for a unified and coordinated mechanism for regular monitoring of all developments to ensure expeditious implementation of measures safeguarding citizens’ interests. He also directed to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families. Keeping in mind the requirements for the fertilizers for the Rabi season, the usage of alternate sources of fertilizers were discussed during the meeting.Mr Modi underlined that all measures must be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers. The Prime Minister further stressed that all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict. He also emphasized the usage of renewable energy sources, in order to ensure energy independence. Mr Modi noted that a whole of government approach will be continued to be adopted to tackle the challenges arising due to the crisis.During the meeting, the Cabinet Secretary briefed the committee about initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products. This was the 4th special CCS meeting on the issue.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, Government is continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. In a video message on social media, Mr Modi said, for the past several decades, every state government and the Central Government have faced the problem of paper leaks, and this has put the future of students at risk.He said, keeping all this in mind, reforms in the education and examination system have become essential across the country, both in the states and at the Centre. The Prime Minister said Parliament has passed the bill containing stringent legal provisions.He highlighted that a transparent, technology-driven examination system, stronger anti-paper leak laws and tough action against exam mafias are important to protect students’ hard work and strengthen the foundation of a Viksit Bharat.

. The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has killed more than 1,500 people in eastern Congo so far. According to official data released by the Congolese government today, the death toll has risen by 50 per cent in about a week, indicating that the outbreak continues to outpace response efforts. The latest update shows that, as of Tuesday, 3,442 cases have been recorded in the current outbreak, and 1,521 people have died.The outbreak, declared on 15th of May, is unlike most previous Ebola outbreaks because the Bundibugyo virus responsible for it has no approved vaccines or treatments. It has also claimed more lives at a faster rate than any previous Ebola outbreak, including the 2014-2016 epidemic, which was considered the deadliest on record, with more than 11,000 deaths among at least 28,000 cases. That outbreak took about eight months to reach 1,000 deaths.Ebola is a rare but highly contagious disease that spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as vomit, blood, or semen. The illness it causes is severe and is often fatal.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that India’s merchandise exports have registered 15 per cent growth so far in the current financial year, despite the Red Sea crisis and global turmoil.He said that despite these headwinds, India’s merchandise exports have grown by 15 per cent during the April-July period. Delivering the JRD Tata Memorial Lecture 2026, Mr Goyal said the country’s merchandise exports remained resilient despite mounting geopolitical tensions and disruptions to global trade routes.The Minister said India’s export performance reflects the strength of the country’s economic fundamentals, even as businesses worldwide grapple with uncertainty stemming from conflicts in West Asia and disruptions in key shipping corridors.The Minister said the first quarter of the current financial year has been marked by persistent global challenges, including volatility in crude oil, petrol, diesel and gas markets, as well as uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and the continuing Red Sea crisis.Highlighting India’s broader economic performance, Mr Goyal said the country remained the world’s fastest-growing major economy, recording 7.7 per cent growth in the previous financial year despite a lot of uncertainty around the world.

Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia today reviewed the progress of the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) in New Delhi and reiterated the government’s commitment to making India a global leader in 6G technologies. The review focused on the progress made by the Bharat 6G Alliance towards achieving Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of making India a front-line contributor in the design, development and deployment of 6G technology by 2030. The Alliance is working through seven specialised groups covering areas such as spectrum, technology, applications, sustainability, manufacturing, outreach and 6G use cases.On the occasion, Mr Scindia stressed the need to benchmark India’s 6G progress against global developments and strengthen collaboration among the Alliance’s working groups. He emphasised that India’s 6G journey must be driven by indigenous research, global standards participation, domestic manufacturing and strong partnerships among government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions.
